title: Runaway tool-argument guard and print-mode CLI inputs in bake-rs
note: Both arms are bake-rs -p from clean release builds: the base at the PR base (bd7d598e54) and the candidate at 6461c965f0 (PR #212), which adds the whitespace-runaway guard to bake-ai's Responses, Chat Completions, and Anthropic stream processors (maxToolArgumentWhitespace, default 2000) and Pi's print-mode CLI inputs (@file, --system-prompt, --append-system-prompt, --no-context-files, --models, prompt templates, and others). The evaluator passes none of the new flags, so the standard suite measures the guard and any change to the default request: the system prompts of all 144 pairs match once the executable and temporary paths are normalized, and each model's first no_tools request has the same size in both arms. Every cliproxyapi model ran through the gateway Pi's CLIProxyAPI provider uses (EVAL_GATEWAY), with gemini-3.8-flash-high at medium effort in place of gemini-3.8-flash-medium, as in the earlier native records; DeepSeek ran on its own API. No regressions. gpt-6.1-sol failures 5 -> 2: all five base failures are the whitespace runaway inside an edit call's arguments reaching the 180 s wall-clock limit after 45 KB to 652 KB of arguments; both candidate failures are the same runaway stopped by the guard (runawayAbort) at about 2,150 characters, 13 and 20 s into the sample. The guard classifies the error as retryable, but the evaluator turns agent retry off, so those samples still fail here. The one gemini base failure is a gateway socket closed before any response byte.

settings.effort: medium where the model offers it; DeepSeek runs at high, its default, having no medium

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
